name: Variable Ratio Write
summary: Own 100 shares and sell two calls at DIFFERENT strikes (one near the money, one further out), widening the profit plateau versus a plain ratio write. Still one uncovered call.
max_profit: achieved between the two strikes: (lower strike - basis + total credits) x 100
max_loss: UNDEFINED above the upper strike; downside is basis - credits
breakevens: lower: basis - total credits; upper: upper strike + total profit at the plateau

greeks.delta: +30 to +45 at entry, turning negative above the upper strike

when_to_use: Historical structure from the pre-electronic era for range-bound stocks with rich IV. FLAGGED: same level-4 problem as the ratio write, with a slightly friendlier payoff shape. Included for completeness only.
entry_rules: BLOCKED at level 3 for the same reason as the ratio write.
At level 4: strikes separated by at least 1.5 x ATR(14); combined credit >= 3% of spot.
Preferred conversion: buy a third, further-OTM call to cap the uncovered leg, converting the structure to covered call + call credit spread, which IS level 3.
management_rules: Convert to defined risk on any move of 1 x ATR(14) toward the upper strike.
No rolling of the uncovered leg upward.
exit_rules: Flatten all short calls by 15:30 ET on expiration day.
Immediate close if total short call delta exceeds 1.20 per 100 shares.
assignment_risk: Assignment on the uncovered upper call produces short stock. Assignment on the lower call delivers the shares, leaving the upper call fully naked - a two-stage failure mode that is worse than a plain ratio write.
buying_power: Naked call margin on the uncovered leg; level 4 only.
common_mistakes: Assuming the wider plateau reduces tail risk - it does not, it only moves the cliff.
family: Stock/ETF Shares Combined With Options (covered writes, protective hedges, collars, synthetics, repairs, conversions)
blocked_because: needs Alpaca options level 4; this account is level 3. Alpaca rejects it with 'account not eligible to trade uncovered option contracts'. Raising the level is an Alpaca approval, not a code change.
